title: Third-party inventory and criticality tiering
status_rationale: SOC2-013 requires inventory of critical services and subservice organizations; RR-REQ-X-073-r2 requires a critical-vendor register; UNB-XIN-SAS-011 requires the subprocessor register be generated from the vendor inventory. No Echelon vendor inventory was located. Business plan section 12.02 (vendor governance) is a draft whose body is a generic template shared across sections and contains no vendor-specific rules.
target_answer: Echelon keeps one vendor inventory that is the source for the subprocessor register, the SBOM-linked open-source inventory and the AI provider list. Each entry records service, data classes accessed, integration points, contract, owner, inherent risk tier and criticality to each customer-facing service. Tiering criteria are documented (data sensitivity, operational criticality, substitutability, regulatory relevance) and applied consistently. The inventory is reconciled quarterly against spend, contracts, identity provider integrations, network egress destinations and code dependencies, so unrecorded vendors surface automatically.
intended_practice: Create the inventory before any production deployment and generate the subprocessor register from it.
customer_statement: Echelon has not yet established its vendor inventory or tiering. It plans a single inventory that drives its subprocessor list, with documented tiering criteria and automated reconciliation.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon vendor risk owner)
residual_risks: Free-tier or individually purchased tools may escape spend-based reconciliation.

title: Pre-engagement vendor due diligence proportional to risk
status_rationale: SOC2-013 and SOC2-030 require due diligence and design review before new external APIs; RR-REQ-X-073-r2 requires assurance type and report period recording. No due diligence procedure or record exists.
target_answer: Before a vendor is engaged or integrated, Echelon performs due diligence scaled to tier: for critical vendors, security assurance (SOC 2 Type 2 or equivalent with CUEC mapping), financial condition, ownership and sanctions screening, legal and regulatory standing, business continuity, subcontractor reliance and data location; for low-risk vendors, a short record. Integration with a new vendor is technically blocked until the inventory entry and approval exist: new egress destinations, OAuth applications and dependencies need an approved vendor record. Neither engineers nor AI agents can add a data-processing vendor on their own.
intended_practice: Implement a tiered due diligence checklist and tie it to the SOC2-030 design review gate.
customer_statement: Echelon plans tiered vendor due diligence before engagement, with technical blocks on unapproved integrations. No due diligence procedure is yet in place.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon vendor risk owner)

title: Vendor contract requirements, including flow-through of customer and regulator rights
status_rationale: No vendor contract standards or executed vendor contracts were reviewed. Unbound requirements expect sponsor regulatory and audit needs to be supported but do not define Echelon's own vendor contract terms.
target_answer: Contracts with vendors that touch customer data or critical services include: security obligations and right to assess; breach notification fast enough for Echelon to meet its own commitments (for example the bank service provider notice under the 2021 computer-security incident rule and 72-hour service provider notice under amended Regulation S-P); audit and regulator examination access that flows to Echelon's regulated customers; data use limits including no AI training; subcontractor approval; data location; business continuity and SLAs; and termination assistance with data return and deletion certification. A contract template and a gap register record where a vendor's standard terms fall short and who accepted the gap.
intended_practice: Draft a vendor contract standard and gap register before first critical vendor engagement for a production service.
customer_statement: Echelon has not yet established vendor contract standards. It plans to require notification, audit, data-use, subcontracting and exit terms that allow it to meet obligations to regulated customers.
residual_risks: Large cloud and AI providers rarely accept negotiated terms; gaps must be risk-accepted and compensated.
open_questions: Which current vendors (cloud, source hosting, AI providers) are under standard click-through terms only?

title: Ongoing monitoring of vendors, assurance report review and CUEC operation
status_rationale: CNV-GOV-002 specifies SOC report gap computation, bridge letters treated as management assertions, stale-report alerts at 12 months, and tracking of exceptions and unmapped CUECs, with release 1 performing this as an annual review task. RR-REQ-X-073-r2 requires every CUEC mapped to an internal control owner before a vendor is marked Assured and allows AI only to extract report metadata for human confirmation. None is operating.
target_answer: Critical vendors are monitored continuously for signals (status pages, breach disclosures, security advisories, ownership changes, financial distress) and reviewed formally at least annually. SOC reports are reviewed for scope, period, opinion, exceptions and CUECs; every CUEC is mapped to an Echelon control with an owner and evidence; bridge letters are recorded as management assertions that do not extend assurance; stale or qualified reports trigger compensating procedures or time-limited risk acceptance. Event triggers (breach, outage, ownership change, scope change) force out-of-cycle review. Issues are tracked to closure.
intended_practice: Run the CNV-GOV-002 annual review task from first vendor engagement; automate gap tracking later.
customer_statement: Echelon plans annual and event-triggered review of critical vendors, including SOC report and CUEC analysis, with continuous signal monitoring. Not yet operating.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon vendor risk owner)

challenge.customer_intent: Customers want assurance that their vendor's vendors remain secure and reliable over time, not just at onboarding.
challenge.adverse_outcome: A critical vendor's controls degrade or it is breached and Echelon does not react.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Annual questionnaires sent to vendors are widely regarded as low-signal: answers are self-reported and dated, and large providers decline custom questionnaires.
challenge.legally_required: Not law for Echelon. Interagency Guidance expects banks to monitor third parties; banks expect their service providers to oversee subcontractors.
challenge.contractually_required: Bank and broker-dealer customers commonly require subcontractor oversight.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Exposure to some vendors can be reduced structurally: minimize data shared, encrypt with Echelon-held keys where feasible, and design for vendor substitution.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Signal feeds and assurance report expiry tracking.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Continuous signal log and CUEC control evidence.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Assurance-report analysis with mapped CUECs plus continuous external signals and data minimization, instead of custom annual questionnaires to large providers.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Review records, CUEC mappings and signal logs are inspectable.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Vendors without assurance reports still need direct assessment.
challenge.alternative_risks: External rating services can be noisy and opaque.
supporting_arguments: CUEC mapping closes the most common reliance gap.

agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Likely; regulators and auditors recognize SOC report review as stronger than questionnaires.'; institutional acceptance rating 'likely' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Small vendors lack reports; questionnaires remain necessary for them.
Signal feeds cost money and produce false positives.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

history.change: BL-021: set institutional_acceptance to unknown (prior 'likely' was unsourced agent judgment, kept in supporting_arguments) and added an unvalidated-acceptance note to opposing_arguments (OBJ-VRM-019, OBJ-SKEPTIC-014).

title: Concentration risk and fourth-party visibility
status_rationale: UNB-CTL-006 requires modelling vendor data restrictions and correlated AI failures; SOC2-022 requires subservice organization controls where relevant; CNV-GOV-002 tracks coverage gaps. No concentration or fourth-party analysis exists.
target_answer: Echelon maps which customer-facing services depend on each critical vendor and on that vendor's own critical providers (fourth parties), including carve-out subservice organizations named in vendor SOC reports. It measures concentration on single cloud regions, single AI providers and single identity or source-hosting providers, records the impact of each failing, and sets tolerances. Where a single provider is accepted, the exit plan and degraded-mode design (for example deterministic paths continuing without AI) are the mitigation.
intended_practice: Produce a dependency map from the vendor inventory and vendor SOC report subservice sections.
customer_statement: Echelon has not yet analyzed vendor concentration or fourth-party dependencies. It plans to map them and to design critical paths to keep working when an AI provider is unavailable.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon vendor risk owner)

title: Exit and termination plans for critical vendors
status_rationale: CNV-GOV-009 requires commercial licences plus escrow or fork rights for release-1 production dependencies; business plan section 12.04 (continuity and exit) is a generic template draft. UNB-OPS-001 requires support for vendor failure. No exit plan exists.
target_answer: Each critical vendor has a written exit plan: trigger conditions, alternate provider or in-house fallback, data export format, migration steps, time to exit, cost estimate and owner. Architecture favors substitutability: standard PostgreSQL managed by Strata rather than proprietary databases, provider-neutral AI interfaces with deterministic fallbacks, infrastructure as code. Exit plans for the most critical vendors are rehearsed (data export and restore on an alternate provider) on a defined cadence. Termination includes credential revocation, data return and deletion confirmation.
intended_practice: Write exit plans for cloud hosting and AI providers before production.
provable: Nothing. Strata exists as a declarative PostgreSQL schema tool in pilot status, supporting PostgreSQL 16 only.
customer_statement: Echelon plans documented and rehearsed exit plans for critical vendors and an architecture that favors substitutable providers. No exit plans exist yet.

challenge.customer_intent: Customers and regulators want assurance that failure or termination of a vendor will not strand the service.
challenge.adverse_outcome: A critical provider fails, changes terms or exits, and the service cannot continue or migrate in time.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Written exit plans are often never tested and decay; their value lies in rehearsal and in architecture that makes exit feasible.
challenge.legally_required: Not law for Echelon in the US. For EU financial entity customers, DORA requires exit strategies for ICT services supporting critical functions, which those customers will flow down.
challenge.contractually_required: Often required by bank and EU financial customers.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Substitutable architecture reduces lock-in: open-standard database, infrastructure as code, provider-neutral AI interfaces.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Automated export and restore to an alternate environment as a scheduled job.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Rehearsed automated migration paths for the top dependencies instead of document-only exit plans for every vendor.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Rehearsal records show actual time and completeness.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Some managed services have no practical alternative at equal capability.
challenge.alternative_risks: Maintaining portability limits use of provider-specific features.
supporting_arguments: agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Likely; tested exits are stronger than documents.'; institutional acceptance rating 'likely' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Rehearsal costs time for a small team.
Customers may still require a document for every critical vendor.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

title: Third-party risk program governance aligned to the Interagency Guidance lifecycle
status_rationale: Unbound control matrix has vendor risk controls UNB-CTRL-082 to 084 (status Designed; no operating evidence). SOC2-013 covers inventory, due diligence, contracts and monitoring. Business plan section 12.02 (vendor governance) is a draft whose body is a generic template shared across sections and contains no vendor-specific rules. No adopted TPRM policy exists.
target_answer: An approved third-party risk policy defines the lifecycle used by Echelon (planning, due diligence and selection, contract negotiation, ongoing monitoring, termination) with governance across it (oversight, accountability, documentation, independent review), mirroring the stages of the 2023 Interagency Guidance so bank customers can map Echelon's practice to their own. It names the accountable owner and risk acceptance authority, sets reporting to leadership, and is independently reviewed. Echelon provides customers the information they need for their own oversight of Echelon as a third party, including its subcontractor oversight.
intended_practice: Adopt a TPRM policy based on the Interagency Guidance lifecycle when Echelon prepares for its first regulated customer.
customer_statement: Echelon has not yet adopted a third-party risk management policy. It plans a program aligned to the Interagency Guidance lifecycle and will provide customers the information needed to oversee Echelon as their third party.
residual_risks: Independent review of the TPRM program is difficult for a very small organization without external help.
